subject: Genomic SEM resource allocation / constraining CPU and RAM usage

messages.author: a01a26b6ad3d73df
messages.subject: Genomic SEM resource allocation / constraining CPU and RAM usage
parts:
Dear Genomic SEM team,

I tried to run Genomic SEM models with SNP effects on an Ubuntu Virtual Machine, though the RAM load of the SNP including Genomic SEM models caused the VM trouble, ultimately "killing" the process and disconnecting the VM. It would be great to get your advice on how to handle this issue, e.g. to manage or limit the R / Genomic SEM computational / memory load, so that the R processes run smoothly. I suppose one "element" within the Genomic SEM package is to switch "parallel" processing on/off and experiment with the "cores", though, so far, it didn't work. 

With many thanks, 
Ulrich

messages.author: a01a26b6ad3d73df
messages.subject: Re: Genomic SEM resource allocation / constraining CPU and RAM usage
parts:
Hi Andrew,

thank you for the quick reply, and I screened the post you mentioned before. There were a couple of useful hints there in respect to the model, the hardware resources and also related to tweaking / "reducing" the model (e.g. to focus on a subset of SNPs or limit the "search" to specific regions of the genome). In respect to resources for non-SNP effect models I had no issues and all steps / models ran in a few minutes.

So, I will do two things. First, reduce the analysis required, i.e. focus on specific SNP subsets and genomic regions. And second, scale up the resources, and see if a more powerful / scale-able VM setup ("Scale Sets") will solve the problem. Hopefully, with the second measure, I can at least run simpler models in a reasonable amount of time and without process interruptions.

In addition, it would be helpful, if you could share some thoughts on the "cores" and "parallel" options in the commonfactor model with SNPs, e.g. in respect to computational / speed differences and resource usage (for example if you examples from test runs / case studies).  

Thank you, 
Ulrich

messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: Genomic SEM resource allocation / constraining CPU and RAM usage
parts:
Hi Ullrich,

One method that ALWAYS works is to run the GWAS per chromosome, or even part of a chromosome of different VM’s/ machines.

The GWAS step doesn’t need to be run on the entire genome.

With respect to guidance on run times that’s beyond the time we have available, especially since the optimal choice will depend heavily on your hardware setup.

Best,
Michel
